n44a20b6ea46.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyaan spacecraft:
1. The Orbital Module is the Crew Module and the Service Module joined together.
2. The Crew Module is the crew habitat that survives re-entry and splashdown.
3. The Service Module injects the Orbital Module into orbit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n44a20b6ea46.x: The Orbital Module is Crew Module plus Service Module, and the Crew Module survives re-entry. Statement 3 is wrong: the human-rated LVM3 injects the Orbital Module into orbit; the Service Module gives on-orbit support and de-orbits.

nf601fa938ba.s:
Consider the following statements about China's Tiangong space station:
1. It was completed in 2022.
2. It is owned by China alone.
3. It consists of the Tianhe core module along with Wentian and Mengtian.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nf601fa938ba.x: All three are correct: Tiangong, completed in 2022, is China's alone and has the Tianhe core with the Wentian and Mengtian modules.

nphysics-23-14.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about astronauts in an orbiting satellite?
o: The satellite and the astronaut accelerate towards Earth with the same g
The mass of the astronaut becomes zero
There is no normal force on the astronaut
nphysics-23-14.x: The satellite and astronaut fall together with the same g, so the normal force is zero and the astronaut feels weightless; the astronaut's mass stays the same.

n088341571a4.s: The SBS-3 programme, approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security in November 2024, envisages how many satellites?
n088341571a4.x: SBS-3 has 52 satellites: 21 to be built by ISRO and 31 by private industry.

ne17adef5872.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ISRO's UNNATI programme?
o: It is a nanosatellite assembly and training programme
It is meant for engineers from developing countries
It was launched in 2019 to mark 50 years of UNISPACE-I
It is a summer space-science programme for Class 9 school students
ne17adef5872.x: UNNATI trains developing-country engineers in nanosatellite assembly (2019, 50 years of UNISPACE-I); the Class 9 school programme is YUVIKA.

n8596824be37.s: PSLV-C37 (15 February 2017) placed how many satellites in orbit in a single launch?
n8596824be37.x: PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites: a Cartosat-2 series satellite, two ISRO nanosatellites and 101 foreign nanosatellites.

n5483e0c9101.s: Under the Indian Space Policy 2023, advanced research, deep space missions and human spaceflight are assigned to:
n5483e0c9101.x: The policy keeps advanced research, deep space and human spaceflight with ISRO; NGEs undertake end-to-end space activities such as satellites, launches and services.

n1ef7d3b77d3.s:
Consider the following statements about ISRO under the Indian Space Policy 2023:
1. ISRO is to move out of making operational and commercial satellites and rockets over time.
2. The policy seeks to privatise ISRO and reduce it to a regulatory body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n1ef7d3b77d3.x: ISRO will move out of operational and commercial production to focus on advanced research, deep space and human spaceflight; it will not be privatised or reduced to a regulator.

nd08e9b833ef.s: Under India's space framework, commercialising mature ISRO technologies through industry is the role of:
nd08e9b833ef.x: Commercialising mature ISRO technology is NSIL's role; IN-SPACe is the independent regulator that authorises and promotes non-governmental entities.

n4e47713f6cd.s: IN-SPACe enabled the technology transfer of which launch vehicle to private consortia?
n4e47713f6cd.x: IN-SPACe enabled the transfer of SSLV technology to private consortia; it was not kept restricted to ISRO.

ne02521c606a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the absence of a Space Activities Act in India?
o: Private space entities lack a statutory framework on liability
Private space entities lack a statutory framework on dispute resolution
Private space entities lack sovereign-backed insurance arrangements
Private space entities already have a statutory liability framework
ne02521c606a.x: Without an Act, private entities have no statutory framework on liability, dispute resolution or risk-sharing, and no sovereign-backed insurance.

new.s: The Gaganyaan mission aims to take a crew of three to a low Earth orbit of about:
new.x: Gaganyaan plans to take a crew of 3 to a 400 km low Earth orbit.

new.s: The planned duration of the Gaganyaan crewed mission is:
new.x: Gaganyaan's goal is a 3-day mission for a crew of 3 in a 400 km orbit; 18 days was Shukla's Axiom-4 stay.

new.s: Gaganyaan's first crewed flight H1 is now targeted for:
new.x: The original target (stated 2018) was December 2021; after repeated revisions H1 is now targeted for Q1 2027.

new.s: Which engine, for the L110 stage of the human-rated LVM3, was qualified in three tests?
new.x: The Vikas engine for the L110 stage was qualified in 3 tests (730 s) for HLVM3.

new.s: The TV-D1 test (18 October 2023) demonstrated a Crew Escape System abort at:
new.x: TV-D1 tested a Crew Escape System abort at Mach 1.2, followed by sea recovery.

new.s: In IADT-02 (10 April 2026), how heavy was the module dropped to test Gaganyaan parachutes?
new.x: IADT-02 used a 5.7 t module with 10 parachutes of 4 types; IADT-01 used a 4.8 t module.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vyommitra?
o: It is an AI-enabled half-humanoid robot
It is to fly on the uncrewed G1 flight
It is to fly on the G2 flight
new.x: Vyommitra is an AI-enabled female half-humanoid robot that flies on G1 and G2; calling it male is false.

new.s: In the IADT-01 air-drop test, the 4.8 t crew module was dropped by an IAF:
new.x: IADT-01 (24 Aug 2025) dropped a 4.8 t module from 3 km using an IAF Chinook at SDSC-SHAR.

new.s: The four Gaganyatris named in February 2024 all have which service background?
new.x: All four Gaganyatris are IAF test pilots.

new.s: The Gaganyatris received basic training abroad at the:
o: Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Russia
new.x: Basic training was at the Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Russia, followed by ISRO's Astronaut Training Facility, Bengaluru.

new.s: Axiom-4, which carried Shubhanshu Shukla to the ISS in June 2025, was launched on:
o: Soyuz MS spacecraft on a Soyuz rocket
new.x: Axiom-4 (25 Jun 2025) flew on a SpaceX Dragon atop a Falcon 9.

new.s: Shubhanshu Shukla is known as the:
new.x: Shukla is the first Indian on the ISS and the second Indian in space; Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian in space (1984).

new.s: Which Indian-origin NASA astronaut flew on Soyuz MS-29 in July 2026 for an eight-month mission?
new.x: Anil Menon, an Indian-origin NASA astronaut, flew on Soyuz MS-29 in July 2026 for 8 months.

new.s: The Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, approved in January 2025, will cost about:
new.x: The Third Launch Pad was approved in January 2025 at about Rs 4,000 crore for NGLV and human spaceflight.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IAM, Bengaluru – New ISRO vertical leading Gaganyaan
HSFC, Bengaluru – Astronaut selection and aeromedical tests
new.x: ISTRAC runs the tracking network; HSFC leads Gaganyaan, IAM does selection and aeromedical tests, and Dhanush is Agnikul's private pad.

new.s: India's first analogue space mission at Leh (November 2024) was conducted by ISRO with AAKA and:
new.x: The Leh analogue mission was run with AAKA and IIT Bombay.

new.s: The HOPE analogue habitat (Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration) is located at:
new.x: HOPE is at Tso Kar, Ladakh, chosen for its early-Mars-like conditions.

new.s: Space motion sickness experienced by astronauts is called:
new.x: Space Adaptation Syndrome is space motion sickness; SANS causes optic disc swelling.

new.s: In microgravity, astronauts lose about how much bone mass a month?
new.x: Bone loss in space is about 1–1.5% of bone mass a month.

new.s: The International Space Station is expected to retire around:
new.x: The ISS, inhabited since November 2000, is to retire around 2030.

new.s: BAS-1, the base module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station, is targeted for launch by:
new.x: BAS-1 is targeted by 2028 on LVM3; the full five-module station by 2035.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bharatiya Antariksh Station:
1. It was approved in September 2024.
2. It will have five modules.
3. Its base module will be launched on PSLV.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: BAS was approved in Sep 2024 and will have five modules; BAS-1 goes up on LVM3, not PSLV.

new.s: SpaDeX, a precursor mission for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station, achieved docking on 16 January 2025 after launch on:
new.x: SpaDeX flew on PSLV-C60 and docked on 16 Jan 2025, making India the 4th country to dock.

new.s: Kibo, a module of the International Space Station, was contributed by:
new.x: Kibo is Japan's ISS module; Zarya (1998) was the first module.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gaganyaan Orbital Module?
o: It has three modules like Soyuz and Shenzhou
It consists of the Crew Module and the Service Module
It is put into orbit by HLVM3
Its Service Module burns up after the de-orbit burn
new.x: Gaganyaan has two parts (Crew Module + Service Module); Russia's Soyuz and China's Shenzhou have three modules.

new.s: GSAT-7, the Indian Navy's 'Rukmini' satellite (2013), was launched by:
new.x: GSAT-7 (Rukmini) was launched by Ariane-5, not GSLV.

new.s: GSAT-7R (CMS-03), launched on 2 November 2025 on LVM3-M5, serves the:
new.x: GSAT-7R (CMS-03) is the Indian Navy's satellite that replaces GSAT-7.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: GSAT-7B is the proposed Indian Army satellite; GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A the Air Force and EMISAT the DRDO.

new.s: RISAT-2, launched in April 2009 on PSLV-C12, carried which type of radar?
new.x: RISAT-2 is an X-band Israeli-built radar satellite; RISAT-1 (2012) is C-band and indigenous.

new.s: RISAT-2BR1, launched in December 2019 on PSLV-C48, marked the:
new.x: RISAT-2BR1 flew on PSLV-C48, the 50th PSLV flight.

new.s: Which radar satellite was the co-passenger of ANUSAT on PSLV-C12 (2009)?
new.x: ANUSAT shared PSLV-C12 with RISAT-2 in 2009.

new.s: The Defence Space Research Organisation (DSRO) is the:
o: R&D arm of the Defence Space Agency
new.x: DSRO is the R&D arm of the Defence Space Agency; IN-SPACe authorises private space activity.

new.s: India's tri-service Defence Space Agency was set up in 2019 at:
new.x: The Defence Space Agency was set up in 2019 at Bengaluru.

new.s: TSAT-1A, India's first private-sector-built sub-metre optical satellite, was launched in April 2024 on:
new.x: TSAT-1A was launched on 7 Apr 2024 on a SpaceX Falcon 9 (Bandwagon-1), not on PSLV.

new.s: TSAT-1A was built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic and assembled at TASL's facility in:
new.x: TSAT-1A was assembled at TASL's Vemagal (Karnataka) facility.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about EDUSAT:
1. It is India's first satellite dedicated to education.
2. It was launched on 20 September 2004 on PSLV.
3. It provides two-way satellite communication to classrooms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: EDUSAT (GSAT-3) is India's first education satellite giving two-way links to virtual classrooms; it was launched on GSLV-F01, not PSLV.

new.s: ANUSAT (2009) is known as India's first:
o: Satellite to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform
new.x: ANUSAT of Anna University was India's first university satellite; StudSat was the first pico-satellite.

new.s: Kalamsat-V2 (January 2019) was the first satellite to use which as an orbital platform?
new.x: Kalamsat-V2 by Space Kidz India was the first to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform.

new.s: WESAT, the first satellite fully built by women students, was built by:
o: LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Thiruvananthapuram
new.x: WESAT was built by LBS Institute of Technology for Women and flew on PSLV-C58 POEM-3.

new.s: SATYABAMASAT, launched on PSLV-C34 in June 2016, collected data on:
new.x: SATYABAMASAT was a micro experimental satellite for greenhouse-gas data; solar UV was WESAT's study.

new.s: PSLV-C62 (January 2026) carried how many start-up and academic co-passengers?
new.x: PSLV-C62 carried 15 co-passengers from Indian and foreign start-ups and academic institutions.

new.s: As of 1 January 2026, Indian rockets had launched over how many foreign satellites?
new.x: Over 400 foreign satellites had been launched on Indian rockets by 1 January 2026.

new.s: ISRO's YUVIKA programme is meant for:
new.x: YUVIKA (Yuva Vigyani Karyakram) is for Indian Class 9 students; UNNATI is for developing-country engineers.

new.s: Under India's space FDI policy, the automatic-route limit for satellite components and subsystems manufacturing is:
new.x: Components and subsystems get 100% automatic route; satellites/data up to 74%; launch vehicles and spaceports up to 49%.

new.s: FDI in satellite manufacturing, operation and data products is allowed on the automatic route up to:
new.x: Satellites, their operation and data products get up to 74% automatic; beyond the limit is the government route.

new.s: The Indian Space Policy 2023 was released by the Department of Space on:
new.x: Approved by Cabinet on 6 April 2023 and released by DoS on 20 April 2023.

new.s: Under the Indian Space Policy 2023, space diplomacy and treaty compliance are the responsibility of:
new.x: DoS handles overall policy, international cooperation, space diplomacy and treaty compliance.

new.s: Antrix Corporation, set up in September 1992, followed which business model?
new.x: Antrix was supply-driven, marketing ISRO products; NSIL (2019) is demand-driven.

new.s: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), set up in 2019, is a CPSE under:
new.x: NSIL is a CPSE under the Department of Space, headquartered in Bengaluru.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about IN-SPACe?
o: It is an autonomous single-window agency under DoS
It authorised the first private launch Vikram-S
It approved the Pixxel-led PPP EOS constellation
new.x: IN-SPACe is headquartered at Ahmedabad; NSIL is at Bengaluru.

new.s: GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20), fully funded and owned by NSIL, was launched in November 2024 on:
new.x: GSAT-N2, a Ka-band broadband satellite fully owned by NSIL, went up on a SpaceX Falcon 9.

new.s: GSAT-24 (2022), India's first demand-driven satellite, was launched from:
new.x: GSAT-24 was launched from Kourou, French Guiana; its DTH capacity went to Tata Play.

new.s: India's first private rocket launch, Vikram-S (2022), was developed by:
new.x: Skyroot Aerospace (Hyderabad) launched Vikram-S in Mission Prarambh on 18 Nov 2022.

new.s: Bellatrix Aerospace's green propulsion system, demonstrated on PSLV-C58, was developed under DRDO's:
new.x: It was developed under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) of DRDO; the Technology Adoption Fund is IN-SPACe's.

new.s: Vikram-1, India's first private orbital rocket, was launched on 18 July 2026 in Mission:
new.x: Aagaman = Vikram-1, orbital (2026); Prarambh = Vikram-S, suborbital (2022).

new.s: Bellatrix Aerospace, maker of electric thrusters and green propulsion, is based in:
new.x: Bellatrix is based in Bengaluru, not Hyderabad.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Dhruva Space – First private launch pad Dhanush
Digantara – Space surveillance and debris tracking
GalaxEye – Drishti SAR and optical satellite
new.x: Dhanush is Agnikul Cosmos's pad; Dhruva Space (Hyderabad) makes nanosatellite platforms.

new.s: India's first private satellite integration facility was set up by:
new.x: Ananth Technologies (Hyderabad) set up India's first private satellite integration facility.

new.s: Agnikul Cosmos's private launch pad and its own mission control are located at:
new.x: Agnikul's pad Dhanush and its mission control are at Sriharikota, India's only operational spaceport.

new.s: The Space Activities Bill finalised in May 2025 gives statutory powers to:
new.x: The Bill, finalised in May 2025, boosts private participation and gives statutory powers to IN-SPACe.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about space legislation in India:
1. The draft Space Activities Bill was first put out in 2017.
2. India has enacted a Space Activities Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The draft Bill came in 2017, but India still has no Space Activities Act; the sector runs on policies and guidelines.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's space economy:
1. Its current size is about US$8.4 billion.
2. The IN-SPACe Decadal Vision targets about 8% global share by 2033.
3. The Rs 1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund is managed through NSIL.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The economy is about US$8.4 billion with a target of US$44 billion (~8% share) by 2033; the VC fund is managed through SIDBI, not NSIL.

new.s: The Technology Adoption Fund for the space sector is run by:
new.x: The Technology Adoption Fund is run by IN-SPACe; the Rs 1,000 crore VC fund is managed through SIDBI.

new.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's space-city plan, Lepakshi Space City is meant for:
new.x: Lepakshi is the second space city, for R&D; Tirupati Space City covers launch-vehicle assembly and satellite manufacturing.

new.s: AP Space Policy 4.0 targets an investment of about ____ during 2025-35.
new.x: AP Space Policy 4.0 targets Rs 25,000 crore investment and 5,000 direct + 30,000 indirect jobs.
